featured_reviews.name: Rhea Gursahani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Both my kids, Krrish and Koel have been with Da Vinci Montessori since Dec 2021 and we intend on continuing with the school as long as we are in the city and respective grades are supported by DVM.

Having experienced both the international and Montessori curriculums, I have seen my kids blossom into independent and opinionated individuals who also empathize and understand the situation around them, with the Montessori curriculum.

Koel was 14 months when she joined Da Vinci in the Toddler Class. 3 months ago, some of the students in Koel's class moved onto the Primary section. This also meant that several young kids now came to her class, and my little girl who once was a baby of the class transformed into the big sister. One day, as I was waiting to receive her, I was narrated a very sweet story by her teacher which touched my heart to the deepest levels.

As was informed, when the younger kids wanted something in class, Koel was the first one to notice, and she would stop whatever activity she was doing, to help the young child. One day, a young toddler was thirsty and made a gesture for the same. Koel noticed this from the other end of the class and ran to pour a glass of water for him. After sometime the young tod was thirsty again but instead of figuring what to do, he immediately went to look for Koel and asked her to pour him another glass of water.

Why I chose to share this story is because it very  beautifully depicts the empathy of the elder child and the independence of the younger one which all blossomed with their simple interaction in class. While the curriculum covers the knowledge aspect, it is these interactions of a mixed age classroom that really transform these young children into independent and caring humans.

Being the 2nd child and a COVID era baby, Koel did not enjoy as much Mama playtime and attention that her elder brother did, but, whatever she has learnt be it life skills, motor skills, empathy, language, knowledge has all been from DVM.

When Krrish joined DVM, he was 4.5 years old and we were returning from a post COVID era. If COVID was tough on us, it was worse with the kids who lost their sense of social being. Krrish was always pro learning but online schooling really got him disinterested in the concept of school. However, with the independence of choice given in the Montessori classroom, Krrish's love for school and learning was back. He was able to pick up the concepts quickly and now is a part of the Elementary class.

So while DVM is a beautiful option for Montessori what sets them apart are the people behind it and the genuine care and affection for the children and their well being. While the ideology is traditional the outlook is modern, to enable children to be successful in the fact paced, tech controlled life today!

Even while being a Montessori curriculum, the children are exposed to a variety of activities on par with international schools, such as Art, Speech and Drama, Physical Fitness, Capoeira, Spanish Music, in the Elementary classroom, and Music, Art, Fitness and Yoga in the Primary and Toddler classrooms.

The head of the school, Ms. Ashani, is deeply invested in ensuring that while the kids continue to learn from the Montessori classroom their future is safeguarded too, hence working on several tie ups with prominent big schools and introducing kids to a variety of inter school activities. The sincerity runs top down and the love, concern and nurturing can be seen in all members of the school from the administrator to each of the teachers in the Toddler, Primary and Elemnentary classroom, as well as the Didis!

I couldn't have asked for a better school for my kids! Thank you for making us a part of the DVM family!
